purpose: Hardens the JSONL review-output parser for issue #221 by adding ~570 lines of edge-case tests (malformed JSON, missing/extra fields, unicode/BOM handling, large and file-based inputs), fast-check property-based schema tests, and deterministic seeded fuzz tests, plus a seeded PRNG helper, two fixtures, and a new fast-check devDependency.
riskRationale: The change is confined to the test suite, fixtures, and a lib-only devDependency (fast-check); no production parsing code is modified and all 1127 tests across 46 files pass. The two findings are parser-consistency gaps that the new tests document rather than cause: parseJsonlString fails BOM-prefixed lines that parseJsonlFile and parseReviewOutput accept, and parseReviewOutput rejects executive_summary entries the manual/file parsers support. These have no production impact today but should be reconciled while the parser surface is being hardened.

text: High-quality test-hardening PR: deterministic seeded fuzz/property tests (mulberry32 + fast-check) make CI failures reproducible, real temp-file tests exercise empty/whitespace-only/multi-thousand-line inputs with proper cleanup, and the unicode/BOM fixtures are carefully constructed. The concern is that the new tests hard-code divergent behavior between the exported parsers — parseJsonlString drops a U+FEFF-prefixed line that parseJsonlFile and parseReviewOutput accept (silently flipping a dropped verdict to ready:false), and executive_summary is handled by the manual/file parsers but rejected by the Zod parseReviewOutput — so the inconsistency should be reconciled before it becomes a compatibility contract.

reasoning: Two parser-consistency issues are enshrined by the new tests rather than reconciled: a BOM prefix on any line after the first is a failed line in parseJsonlString but valid in parseJsonlFile/parseReviewOutput (empirically verified: same 3-line input yields failedLines=1/ready:false vs valid=2/ready:true), and executive_summary is accepted by the manual and file parsers but rejected by the Zod parser. Both are small, safe fixes that prevent silent divergence between the exported parser APIs, so they should be landed before this hardening is treated as complete.

message: Property-based tests use fixed seeds (PROPERTY_SEED=0xc0ffee) and the seeded mulberry32 PRNG, with the helper explicitly banning Date.now()-style non-determinism, so any fuzz/property failure is byte-for-byte reproducible in CI.

The 'manual parser and Zod parser agree on valid entries' property test cross-checks parseJsonlString against the Zod-backed parseReviewOutput on the same generated inputs, giving the two parser paths a shared reference oracle.

File-based tests use real temp dirs with try/finally cleanup and cover empty, whitespace-only, BOM-only, 1200-line, and non-existent files, exercising parseJsonlFile's stream/readline path rather than mocking it.

The unicode fixture deliberately covers CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic, single emoji, and ZWJ multi-codepoint family emoji in one small file, pinning down encoding round-tripping that commonly breaks naive JSONL parsers.
fast-check is correctly scoped to lib's devDependencies with the pnpm lockfile updated, keeping the fuzz dependency out of the runtime bundles and the action/app packages.

The new tests hard-code contradictory BOM semantics between the two exported parsers: parseJsonlString (jsonl-parser.ts:228) parses each untrimmed line, so a U+FEFF BOM prefix on any line after the first is a failed line (asserted at line 490), while parseReviewOutput (schemas.ts) and production parseJsonlFile (jsonl-parser.ts:76) trim each line first and accept the identical input (asserted in schema.test.ts:123). Verified empirically: the same 3-line input yields failedLines=1 and verdict.ready=false from parseJsonlString but valid=2 and verdict.ready=true from parseReviewOutput. A BOM-prefixed verdict line is therefore silently dropped by the string parser, and any future switch from file-based to string-based parsing would silently change review outcomes.
suggestion: Make parseJsonlString trim each line before JSON.parse so it matches parseJsonlFile/parseReviewOutput, then update the two BOM tests (this one and schema.test.ts:123) to assert the same tolerant behavior instead of the divergence.

message: parseReviewOutput's Zod ReviewEntrySchema discriminated union only covers summary/verdict/strength/issue, so an executive_summary entry — which both parseJsonlString (jsonl-parser.ts:85) and the production parseJsonlFile route and parse — is reported as invalid, a divergence the new schema.test.ts:141 test explicitly asserts. The two exported review-output parsers disagree on a documented entry type, so if parseReviewOutput is ever promoted to production it would silently discard the executive summary.
suggestion: Add a ReviewExecutiveSummarySchema to the Zod union and route it into a result field (mirroring the manual parser), or document the manual/file parsers as the only executive_summary-capable path.
